pages.title: Coin
pages.text: The coin is the money of Gensokyo. Eight coins make a coin stack; a stack is worth eight coins wherever a price is counted, so it saves inventory space and nothing else.$(br2)Both characters and shelves charge in coins, and the price is paid straight from your inventory — the trade screen shows your purse, and a stack is broken into loose coins only when there are not enough of them. Coins can also be thrown like a danmaku: a thrown coin flies out and lands where it falls, ready to be picked back up.$(br2)A shrine's donation box takes coins too, and pays back a blessing once enough have been given.

$(bold)Trading$()$(br)Talk to a character and open her trades, or use the trade button in the conversation. Her offers are laid out as a board of icons: goods she sells for coins, goods she buys from you, and work she does with materials you bring. A tag under an icon shows the price; a price turned red is more than you carry.$(br2)The buttons on the right filter the board — her wares, her purchases, and her work — and the arrows turn the page. Each offer has a stock; an emptied offer stays on the board but cannot be traded until it restocks. The plate on the left shows how much money you carry.

$(bold)Shelf Offers$()$(br)Rinnosuke keeps the shelves of Kourindou stocked himself. While he is at home he picks a shelf, walks over, and lays out one item from his own catalogue: a price, and a few of the item, different every time. Gifts, drinks, books and odd tools all pass through his hands; the rarer a thing is, the higher he prices it and the fewer he puts out.$(br2)Buy from his shelves as you would from any other: right-click with the coins in your inventory. If you place shelves of your own, he leaves them alone while they hold goods, stock or earnings; a shelf you have emptied completely may be claimed for his shop and restocked with his wares. See $(l:decoration/shelves)Shelves$(/l).
